summary: Draft candidate package for AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power. The clean Win25H2Clean phase-0 batch confirmed the parent key exists while the value is absent on baseline, the repo power notes carry an exact docs hit with literal 1, the targeted current-build string batch found an exact ntoskrnl.exe Unicode hit, the shared mega-trigger runtime lane armed candidate value 1 but recovered without an exact hit, a retained local-KD disassembly pass shows the visible generic power-setting query/store layer operating through PopFindPowerSettingConfiguration, PopPowerSettingChangeStamp, and PopRegisteredPowerSettingCallbacks rather than a visible registry API, and a wildcard KD plus symbol-seeded Ghidra follow-up shows no visible `*PowerRequest*Reg*` helper while the only naturally resolved setting callback is the timeout-specific `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback`. New retained live-state and direct-reader passes now confirm `nt!PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired = 1` and show `PopPowerRequestEvaluateExecutionRequiredStatus` reading that global on the current build. A retained broad lightweight runtime lane also wrote the pair from baseline-missing to candidate value `1`, completed a real soft reboot, and still returned `no-hit` for the pair after reboot. A new retained retry audit over 10 mega-trigger runtime runs shows the pair repeatedly armed from baseline-missing to `1` and then exited `aborted-recovered` with zero exact hits on every parsed retry. A retained runtime path audit over the only current-build `path-hits.csv` capture found zero exact hits for the pair itself but 15 adjacent `Control\Power\PowerRequestOverride` accesses by `svchost.exe`, a new override-alignment audit ties those adjacent hits to the already-proven current-build override lineage, and a new power-setting trace-callback audit shows the visible generic setter registering `PopTracePowerSettingChange` rather than an exact pair-specific callback. A refreshed KVM guest-control audit now shows the dedicated narrow runtime runner is already wired, the qemu guest-agent channel is attached on the active libvirt domain, and a live bootstrap attempt installed the official qga MSI plus guest-tools MSI in the guest, confirmed a running `QEMU-GA` service and visible `VIOSERIALPORT` devices. A new live foreground repro then stopped `QEMU-GA`, observed host-side `guest-ping` fall back to `not connected`, and reproduced the stronger `QEMU guest agent is not available due to an error` state by launching `qemu-ga.exe -v -p \\.\Global\org.qemu.guest_agent.0` directly in an admin console. A later open-path probe then proved both `\\.\Global\org.qemu.guest_agent.0` and the exact registry-derived `...&02...` interface path are openable with `CreateFile`, and a follow-up exact-path foreground launch still reproduced the same host-side error/disconnected state while qga ran in a `debug: dispatch` loop. A new runtime-handshake probe then showed the guest-side signal is still quiet even after path discovery is closed: the exact-path qga logfile collapses to repeated `debug: dispatch` lines, recent Application events stay empty, and the host still sees a disconnected/not-connected qga channel. A new host-side socket-state audit then tightened that gate to a pre-protocol attach fault by showing `frontend-open=false`, `guest off, host off`, and `Connection refused` on the qga unix socket. A later live reboot/state capture then refined that blocker again: one retained reboot did show `QEMU-GA` stopped with `WIN32_EXIT_CODE 1067` and a matching System log `terminated unexpectedly`, but a later reboot with the service still configured as ordinary `AUTO_START` came back `RUNNING` on its own while the host side remained unchanged at `frontend-open=true`, `guest on, host off`, `guest-ping` error, and qga unix-socket `Connection refused`. A same-process socket-contrast probe then proved the failure is not a generic host-to-QEMU unix socket limitation: the live libvirt-managed qga socket still returned `ConnectionRefusedError(111, 'Connection refused')`, while a temporary QMP `chardev-add` socket backend at `/tmp/regprobe-qga-socktest.sock` accepted a direct host-side AF_UNIX connection in the same running qemu-system-x86_64 process. A later attached-virtserial contrast then showed the failure is not even generic to virtserialport-attached sockets: a hot-added `virtserialport` named `org.codex.porttest.0` on port 16 accepted a host-side AF_UNIX connection through `/tmp/regprobe-qga-porttest.sock`, while the live qga channel on port 2 still refused the same connect pattern. A same-directory socket contrast then closed the host path theory as well: a temporary QMP socket backend created directly under `/run/user/1000/libvirt/qemu/run/channel/1-regprobe-win11-25h2-/codex.same-dir.sock` accepted a host-side AF_UNIX connection, while the live qga socket beside it still refused one. A later guest-state contrast then showed that refusal survives both service states: stopping `QEMU-GA` flips `guest-ping` from `QEMU guest agent is not available due to an error` to `QEMU guest agent is not connected` and moves `info qtree` from `guest on, host off` to `guest off, host off`, but direct AF_UNIX connect to the live qga socket still returns `ConnectionRefusedError(111, 'Connection refused')` before stop, after stop, and after restart. A later listener-state snapshot then showed the qga path is not simply missing a host listener either: `ss -xlpn` and `lsof -U -a -p <qemu pid>` both show `/run/user/1000/libvirt/qemu/run/channel/1-regprobe-win11-25h2-/org.qemu.guest_agent.0` as a qemu-owned `LISTEN` socket, yet direct host-side connect still returns `ConnectionRefusedError(111, 'Connection refused')`; the sibling qemu monitor socket on the same process instead returns `BlockingIOError(11, 'Resource temporarily unavailable')`. A later live libvirt-channel contrast then closed another generic theory: a temporary `virsh attach-device --live` unix `virtio` channel named `org.codex.libvirttest.0` created a host-connectable socket immediately on the same running domain, while the live qga socket still returned `ConnectionRefusedError(111, 'Connection refused')`. The candidate remains research-only because the earlier Control\Power seeding path and an exact post-boot read are still unresolved, and the live runtime-trace lane is currently environment-gated by a stable qga-specific libvirt/QEMU integration or handshake failure rather than by missing runner design.

setting.name: Allow Audio To Enable Execution Required Power Requests
setting.casual_explanation: This low-level Control\Power value appears to influence whether active audio can contribute to execution-required power-request behavior inside the kernel power-request subsystem.
setting.why_people_change_it: Researchers track it when they want to understand how audio activity participates in execution-required power requests and whether that behavior is registry-seeded or runtime-driven.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The candidate now has enough docs, static, and debugger evidence for a real draft package, and the visible current-build live state plus direct reader path are no longer open questions. A retained broad soft-reboot lane also exists, but it only narrows the missing layer to exact post-boot tracing rather than proving an exact rebooted read. The only retained runtime path-hit CSV currently lands on the adjacent `PowerRequestOverride` subtree rather than on the pair itself, that adjacent subtree now has its own override-lineage alignment proof, and the visible generic setter path now has explicit trace-callback proof rather than pair-binding proof.
setting.professional_notes: The Win25H2Clean 96-key phase-0 existence batch confirmed that HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power exists while AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests itself is absent on the clean baseline. Repo power notes document an exact literal of 1 and map the setting to PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired. The targeted string batch on the current build found an exact Unicode hit in C:\Windows\System32\ntoskrnl.exe for the value name. A shared mega-trigger runtime lane then armed candidate value 1 for AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests but the Procmon export recovered in an aborted state and did not yield an exact read. The retained local-KD power-setting query/store pass disassembled PopQueryPowerSettingUlong, PopGetPowerSettingValue, and PopSetPowerSettingValue. In the retained path, the generic power-setting subsystem acquires PopSettingLock, resolves configuration objects through PopFindPowerSettingConfiguration, updates PopPowerSettingChangeStamp, walks PopRegisteredPowerSettingCallbacks, schedules PopSetNotificationWork, and contains an explicit callback registration site that loads `PopTracePowerSettingChange` into `r8` before calling `PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback`. That retained callsite reinforces that the visible generic setter path is still notification/trace plumbing rather than an exact binding site for the execution-required pair. A second retained wildcard KD pass then showed no visible `nt!*PowerRequest*Reg*` symbols on the current build and only one `nt!*PowerRequest*Setting*` symbol: PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback. The symbol-seeded Ghidra probe on that callback resolved only the timeout GUID path and found no direct or bounded indirect references to the callback symbol itself. New retained local-KD live-state proof now shows `nt!PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired = 1`, matching the repo-doc enabled literal. A retained disassembly pass also shows `PopPowerRequestEvaluateExecutionRequiredStatus` directly comparing `PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired` against zero while it reads `PopExecutionRequiredTimeout` during execution-required evaluation. A retained broad lightweight runtime lane then armed both execution-required values from baseline-missing to candidate value `1`, completed a real `reboot_mode=soft` cycle with healthy shell state before and after reboot, and still reported `no-hit` for both pair members in the post-boot batch result. The only retained current-build runtime `path-hits.csv` capture for this lane also stays adjacent: it contains zero exact hits for AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests and AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests, but 15 `svchost.exe` accesses under `HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power\PowerRequestOverride` covering the root, `Driver`, `Process`, and `Service` subkeys. A new alignment audit then ties those adjacent hits back to the already-proven override family in wildcard KD evidence: `PopPowerRequestHandleRequestOverrideQueryResponse`, `PopPowerRequestOverrideInitialize`, `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideQuery`, and `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideCleanup`, while the retained root dump also contains the `PowerRequestOverride` subtree. Together these follow-ups close the visible live-state and direct-reader gaps, while narrowing the runtime-trace story to an adjacent override lineage and a trace-oriented generic setter rather than exact pair reads. A refreshed host-side KVM guest-control audit then showed the remaining runtime lane is environment-gated in a narrower way: both execution-required records already map to the dedicated narrow path-aware runner, the live libvirt domain exposes the qemu guest-agent channel, and a live bootstrap attempt installed the official qga MSI plus the official `virtio-win-gt-x64.msi`, confirmed a running `QEMU-GA` service and visible `VIOSERIALPORT` devices, and rebooted the guest, yet host-side `guest-ping` still fails with `QEMU guest agent is not available due to an error` while the host-side controller stack remains vmrun-backed. A follow-up foreground repro then stopped `QEMU-GA`, observed host-side `guest-ping` fall back to `Guest agent is not responding: QEMU guest agent is not connected`, and reproduced the stronger `QEMU guest agent is not available due to an error` state by launching `qemu-ga.exe -v -p \\.\Global\org.qemu.guest_agent.0` directly in an admin console. The foreground console printed continuous `debug: dispatch` lines instead of a simple open-path failure, so the blocker now survives both the Windows service wrapper and an explicit expected-port launch. A later open-path probe then removed Windows path resolution as the leading theory: the guest can now open both `\\.\Global\org.qemu.guest_agent.0` and the exact DeviceClasses-derived `...&02...` interface path with `CreateFile`, while the `...&01...` sibling returns access denied and the naive `vport0p2` aliases still stay missing. A follow-up launcher then started `qemu-ga.exe -v -m virtio-serial -p <exact ...&02... path>` from the retained probe output, yet host-side `guest-ping` still returned `QEMU guest agent is not available due to an error` and HMP `info chardev` still showed the qga channel as `disconnected`. A subsequent runtime-handshake probe narrowed the failure again without resolving it: exact-path qga startup still produced only repeated `debug: dispatch` lines in the logfile tail, while recent Windows Application events stayed empty and the host still observed a disconnected/not-connected qga channel. The remaining KVM blocker therefore looks like a silent post-launch qga stall or libvirt/KVM handshake failure, not path discovery. A same-process socket-contrast probe then narrowed the fault one layer further: the live libvirt-managed qga socket still returned `ConnectionRefusedError(111, 'Connection refused')`, while a temporary QMP `chardev-add` unix socket backend at `/tmp/regprobe-qga-socktest.sock` accepted a direct host-side AF_UNIX connection in the same running qemu-system-x86_64 process. That means the persistent failure is not a generic host-to-QEMU unix-socket limitation on the current host. A later attached-virtserial contrast narrowed it one step further: a hot-added `virtserialport` named `org.codex.porttest.0` on port 16 accepted a host-side AF_UNIX connection through `/tmp/regprobe-qga-porttest.sock`, while the live qga channel on port 2 still refused the same connect pattern. The retained fault is therefore specific to the qga channel's live state or libvirt/qga integration path, not to virtserial sockets in general. A same-directory socket contrast then showed the libvirt qemu `run/channel` directory itself is not the source either, because a temporary socket backend in that same directory accepted a host-side connection while the live qga socket still refused one. If this candidate is still registry-backed on the current build, the Control\Power seeding must occur earlier than the visible generic query/store, trace-callback, timeout-setting, direct reader, and adjacent override layers, or the post-boot window must be captured from a restored host-side guest-control surface with a narrower exact-read lane.

decision.why: AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests now has exact repo-doc coverage, clean-baseline absence proof, current-build ntoskrnl string corroboration, a real trigger arm, retained local-KD proof that `PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired = 1`, a direct current-build reader in `PopPowerRequestEvaluateExecutionRequiredStatus`, a retained local-KD view of the generic power-setting query/store layer, retained wildcard/symbolized binding follow-ups, a retained broad soft-reboot runtime lane that still returns `no-hit` after reboot, a retained retry audit showing 10 mega-trigger runtime attempts all ending `aborted-recovered`, a retained path audit showing only adjacent `PowerRequestOverride` activity in the visible runtime CSV layer, a new alignment audit that ties that adjacent subtree back to the current-build override family, a new trace-callback audit showing the visible generic setter registering `PopTracePowerSettingChange` rather than an exact pair binding, and a refreshed host-side KVM guest-control audit showing the remaining narrow runtime lane is now blocked by a guest-side qga runtime/protocol failure after live bootstrap rather than by missing repo plumbing. A new live foreground repro strengthened that blocker by showing the failure survives an explicit expected-port launch. The later open-path diagnosis then closed the remaining path-resolution theory as well: both `\\.\Global\org.qemu.guest_agent.0` and the exact DeviceClasses-derived `...&02...` interface path are openable in the guest, yet restarting `QEMU-GA` or launching qga directly on the exact `...&02...` path still leaves host-side `guest-ping` in `QEMU guest agent is not available due to an error` and HMP `info chardev` in `disconnected`. The follow-up runtime-handshake diagnosis narrowed the failure one step further: even with logfile capture on the exact openable path, the guest-side signal only collapses to repeated `debug: dispatch` lines and no recent matching Application events, while the host still sees a disconnected/not-connected qga channel. A same-process socket-contrast probe then showed the persistent refusal is not a generic host-to-QEMU unix-socket limitation: a temporary QMP `chardev-add` socket backend in the same live qemu-system-x86_64 process accepted a direct AF_UNIX connection immediately, while the live libvirt-managed qga socket still returned `ConnectionRefusedError(111, 'Connection refused')`. A later attached-virtserial contrast then showed the problem is not even generic to virtserialport-attached sockets: a hot-added port 16 `virtserialport` in the same live VM accepted a host-side AF_UNIX connection immediately, while the live qga channel on port 2 still refused one. A same-directory socket contrast then showed the host path prefix is not the issue either: a temporary QMP socket backend created directly inside the same libvirt channel directory accepted a host-side AF_UNIX connection while the live qga socket beside it still refused one. A later guest-state contrast then showed the raw refusal survives both guest-on and guest-off states: stopping `QEMU-GA` flips `guest-ping` to `QEMU guest agent is not connected` and `info qtree` to `guest off, host off`, but direct host-side AF_UNIX connect to the live qga socket still returns `ConnectionRefusedError(111, 'Connection refused')`; starting the service restores `guest on, host off` and the stronger error state with the same refusal. A later listener-state snapshot then narrowed the blocker again: the qga path is already a qemu-owned `LISTEN` socket in both `ss` and `lsof`, yet direct host-side connect still returns `ConnectionRefusedError(111, 'Connection refused')`, while the sibling qemu monitor socket on the same process behaves differently and returns `BlockingIOError(11, 'Resource temporarily unavailable')`. A later live libvirt-channel contrast then showed the refusal is not generic to libvirt-managed unix `virtio` channels either: a temporary `virsh attach-device --live` channel created a host-connectable socket immediately on the same running domain, while the live qga socket still refused. The restored bootstrap ISO removes the missing-media issue and the guest now reaches a stronger post-bootstrap state, but the unresolved layer is now qga-specific libvirt/QEMU integration or handshake behavior rather than generic libvirt channel wiring, simple listener absence, or Windows path discovery, so that still does not restore live host-side execution on its own.
blocking_issues: The visible generic power-setting query/store layer is in-memory and callback-driven, but the earlier Control\Power seeding path into PopFindPowerSettingConfiguration objects or execution-required globals is still unresolved.

The only naturally resolved setting callback is tied to GUID_EXECUTION_REQUIRED_REQUEST_TIMEOUT and PopExecutionRequiredTimeout rather than to an exact AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests binding site.
A retained broad soft-reboot lane now exists, but it still produced only batch-level `no-hit` rather than an exact post-boot read for AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests.

A retained retry audit over 10 mega-trigger runtime attempts shows the trigger family is no longer missing; it repeatedly arms the pair from baseline-missing to `1` but still exits `aborted-recovered` without an exact registry read for AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests.

The only retained current-build runtime `path-hits.csv` capture shows adjacent `Control\Power\PowerRequestOverride` accesses by `svchost.exe` and zero exact path hits for AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests itself.

A retained alignment audit now links those adjacent runtime hits to the visible current-build override family rather than to an exact execution-required pair read, which strengthens the case that the missing layer is earlier seeding or a narrower exact-read lane.
A retained trace-callback audit shows the visible generic `PopSetPowerSettingValue` callback registration targets `PopTracePowerSettingChange`, not an exact execution-required pair binding site.

The dedicated narrow runtime lane is already mapped, and the active KVM session has the qemu guest-agent channel attached. Live bootstrap installed qga plus guest-tools, `QEMU-GA` can be started, the default alias `\\.\Global\org.qemu.guest_agent.0` is openable, and the exact DeviceClasses-derived `...&02...` path is also openable, but host-side `guest-ping` still fails with `QEMU guest agent is not available due to an error` and HMP still reports the qga chardev as `disconnected`. Even a foreground `qemu-ga.exe -v -m virtio-serial -p <exact ...&02... path>` launch reproduces the same failure, and the later runtime-handshake probe adds only repeated `debug: dispatch` log lines plus no recent matching Application events. A same-process socket-contrast probe then showed a temporary QMP socket backend in the same live qemu process accepts host-side AF_UNIX connects while the live qga socket still returns `ConnectionRefusedError(111, 'Connection refused')`. A later attached-virtserial contrast showed the same thing one layer closer to qga: a hot-added `virtserialport` on port 16 accepts a host-side AF_UNIX connection while the live qga channel on port 2 still refuses one. A same-directory socket contrast then showed the libvirt qemu `run/channel` directory itself is not the cause: a temporary socket backend in that same directory accepts a host-side connection while the live qga socket beside it still refuses one. A later guest-state contrast then showed the raw refusal survives both service states: stopping `QEMU-GA` flips `guest-ping` to `QEMU guest agent is not connected` and `info qtree` to `guest off, host off`, yet the same direct host-side socket connect still refuses; starting the service again restores `guest on, host off` plus the stronger error state with the same refusal. A later listener-state snapshot then showed the qga path is not simply unbound on the host either: `ss` and `lsof` both show it as a qemu-owned `LISTEN` socket, but direct host-side connect still returns `ConnectionRefusedError(111, 'Connection refused')`, while the sibling qemu monitor socket on the same pid returns `BlockingIOError(11, 'Resource temporarily unavailable')`. A later live libvirt-channel contrast then showed the refusal is not generic to libvirt-managed unix `virtio` channels either: a temporary `virsh attach-device --live` channel creates a host-connectable socket immediately on the same running domain, while the live qga socket still refuses. The repo controller stack therefore remains environment-gated by qga-specific libvirt/QEMU integration or handshake behavior rather than by missing path discovery, simple listener absence, guest open state, or generic libvirt unix channel behavior.

open_questions: Is AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests seeded earlier into execution-required state during boot or resume, or does the modern current-build family leave the Control\Power value absent while keeping only the in-memory global at `1` and the adjacent `PowerRequestOverride` subtree as the only visible runtime registry activity?

Should the next decisive step target qga-specific libvirt/QEMU integration behavior directly, or should the same narrow runtime lane be executed from a vmrun-capable environment that bypasses the current KVM qga channel?
